title: Paku Dipukul Miring ke Balok Keras Tetap Lurus
hook: Paku dipukul miring ke balok kayu keras sampai kepala rata dan batangnya tetap lurus saat dicabut
story: Di meja kerja bengkel kayu, satu kardus Paku Cap Keris sudah terbuka sejak frame pertama di sisi kanan meja dengan garis hijau dan cetakan CAP KERIS menghadap kamera, ditemani tumpukan kecil paku baja bersih. Tukang kayu menusukkan satu paku agak miring ke balok kayu keras, memukul kepalanya sampai rata tanpa batang membengkok, lalu mencabutnya dengan catut dan mengangkat paku itu ke samping kardus untuk memperlihatkan batangnya masih lurus. Penutup: ia meletakkan paku lurus itu di meja sambil mengangguk tenang dan mengarahkan penonton bertanya ukuran lewat DM tanpa nomor WhatsApp.
caption:
Paku dipukul miring ke balok kayu keras dan batangnya tetap lurus sampai kepala rata. Mau tanya ukuran paku yang pas untuk bekisting? Tanya lewat DM aja.

shots.prompt: Photorealistic live-action video, vertical 9:16, 10 seconds, one continuous take, shot on smartphone vlog camera held at chest height across a carpenter workbench with gentle natural handheld sway and a slight low angle, natural clean daylight neutral white balance, true-to-life colors, realistic matte human skin with visible fine pores, no plastic shine, no waxy skin, no glass skin, no yellow or orange tint, no artificial golden glow, zero CGI, authentic non-AI documentary look, clean frame without camera HUD, no REC icon, no viewfinder brackets, no camera display overlay, no on-screen text or captions of any kind. Location: a simple Indonesian carpentry workshop, one scarred hardwood workbench with sawdust, bright overcast daylight from a side window. From the very first frame one open kraft carton of Paku Cap Keris from the single attached official reference photo stands at the right edge of the bench with its green stripe and black CAP KERIS print facing the camera, and a small pile of clean straight steel nails lies beside it. An Indonesian male carpenter about 45 years old in a faded grey work shirt with rolled sleeves, dark work trousers and a worn field cap stands behind the bench; his face, hands and torso stay in frame the whole take. PROP CONTINUITY RULE: from 0.0s to 10.0s exactly one open nail carton on the right, one wooden-handled hammer in his right hand, one hardwood block in the middle of the bench, one pair of pincers resting near the block and one nail being driven are the props; no extra tool, person, plank, bucket, machine, animal or second carton may appear, move in, fall or disappear at any instant, the carton print and its green stripe must not change, and the hammer must never be swapped. BEATS: from 0.0s to 0.5s he already holds the hammer raised over one nail set at a slight angle in the hardwood block. From 0.5s to 4.8s he strikes the nail head twice with firm controlled blows while turning his head to the camera and says in clear Indonesian: "Paku dipukul miring ke balok keras tetap lurus." From 4.8s to 5.4s he drives the nail flush with two short strikes, the shaft staying perfectly straight. From 5.5s to 9.2s he grips the nail with the pincers, pulls it out and holds it up beside the open carton with its black CAP KERIS print facing camera while saying in clear Indonesian: "Paku Cap Keris PT Intan Suar Kartika kuat." From 9.2s to 9.7s he lowers the straight nail onto the bench and gives one calm nod, the nail still straight and visible in the final frame beside the carton.
